candidates.text: I’ve always had a strong sense of direction. That was the problem. What if after 7 long days trudging through the deep woods, you discovered the compass that had been guiding your every step was actually broken? You’d realize you were lost. It wasn’t until 7 years into my creative career that I discovered I was utterly and completely lost. I was operating with a broken compass. candidates.text: ​NOWNESS Shorts: Der Mann und sein Haus Constructing a celebration of stillness and the cinematic form, Indian-born filmmaker Kriti Dale explores the act of being present by stripping life to its essentials for the short film Der Mann und sein Haus – translated as The Man and His House . Through the life of 70-year-old Chi-Gong teacher Lambert in Uckermark, North Eastern Germany, the film presents a visual essay on self-sufficiency as both philosophy and daily practice, and the contentment found in mundane tasks. Against the endless skies and rusting birch trees of rural Brandenburg, Lambert chops wood, tends fire, cooks, and cleans the house built with his own hands, finding purpose in unadorned surroundings, and an appreciation of simplicity, quiet, and discipline. - Kriti Dale Working entirely in available light, with the camera held at a fixed distance, Dale shot on Kodak 500T 16mm film – overexposed and pull-processed to enhance the textures of solitude, from the rich blackness of night, to the soft highlights of open fire and daylight. Building the film around ambient sound – the hum of work and countryside, the call of the region’s native cranes, the crackle of the fire – Dale creates distance from the modern urban world beyond the frame, immersing viewers in a life of chosen stillness with just one lingering question: can a man truly be an island?
